parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Standard electrode potentials can be used to compare the stability of different complex ions for a given transition element.

Table 4.1 lists electrode potentials for some electrode reactions for $\text{Fe}^{3+}/\text{Fe}^{2+}$ systems.

Table 4.1

| electrode reaction | $E^\ominus/\text{V}$ |
| :--- | :--- |
| $[\text{Fe(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{3+} + \text{e}^- \rightleftharpoons [\text{Fe(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{2+}$ | +0.77 |
| $[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]^{3-} + \text{e}^- \rightleftharpoons [\text{Fe(CN)}_6]^{4-}$ | +0.36 |
| $[\text{Fe(bipy)}_3]^{3+} + \text{e}^- \rightleftharpoons [\text{Fe(bipy)}_3]^{2+}$ | +0.96 |

Use relevant data from Table 4.1 to state which iron(III) complex is hardest to reduce. Explain your choice.
